experience.title: Data Engineering Intern
bullets: Built a data curation tool and lakehouse workflows so teams could reliably work with tens of thousands of new images and their metadata every day without manual wrangling.
Organized storage and query layers on AWS (object storage + query engines + table formats) to make experiments reproducible instead of "one-off" scripts.
Instrumented the flows and dashboards so stakeholders could see health and trends at a glance, which also helped us cut repetitive ETL.
Integrated the pipeline with our ML tracking so models could be trained on consistent versions of the data and compared fairly.

experience.title: Undergraduate Teaching Assistant — Python
bullets: Ran weekly labs and live code-along sessions that turned abstract concepts—like data structures and OOP—into small, testable programs students could extend.
Focused on removing "mystery" from debugging by teaching a structured approach: isolate, verify, refactor.
Gave targeted feedback on projects to improve clarity, performance, and style, so students left with habits they could apply beyond the course.
Helped more students ship working code confidently and on time.

experience.title: Software Engineer Intern
bullets: Designed and shipped backend features that real users touched every day, starting from clean API contracts and ending with observable, deployable services.
Tightened data access patterns and added caching so common requests were fast and predictable under load, not just on my laptop.
Built auth and rate-limiting around the APIs to protect the system as traffic grew.
Delivered a service that felt snappier to users and easier for the team to operate.
